tests.title: Global shortcut reads the current selection and preserves the clipboard
tests.user_story: As a desktop user, I can select text in another app and invoke Tristr Flow without disturbing my clipboard.
setup_instrumentation: Run the packaged macOS app with Accessibility granted.
Put a unique non-text item or sentinel text on the clipboard.
Keep main-process logs visible for shortcut and selection diagnostics.
steps: Select a known sentence in TextEdit or Chrome.
Confirm the overlay opens, shows the exact selected sentence, and starts audio.
Confirm the prior clipboard value is restored.
expected_results: Both registered shortcuts invoke selection capture.
The overlay content matches the selected text.
Clipboard contents are unchanged after capture.

tests.title: Read selected text works from the tray menu
tests.user_story: As a user whose shortcut is unavailable, I can still read the current selection from the menu-bar dropdown.
setup_instrumentation: Run the packaged macOS app with Accessibility granted.
Open a document containing a unique sentence.
steps: Open the Tristr Flow tray menu without changing the document selection.
Confirm the overlay opens with the exact sentence and audio begins.
expected_results: The menu item is prominent near the top of the action section.
It uses selection capture rather than existing clipboard text.
The same speech workflow runs as the keyboard shortcut.
proof_to_capture: Overlay screenshot with the selected sentence

tests.title: Broken shortcut or Accessibility state is visible and recoverable
tests.user_story: As a user, I receive an obvious fallback when macOS permission or shortcut registration is unhealthy.
setup_instrumentation: Use a controlled build with Accessibility disabled, then repeat with a configured shortcut held by a helper Electron process.
Inspect the tray menu before and after restoring each condition.
steps: Open the tray menu while Accessibility is unavailable.
Confirm Read selected text is warning-highlighted and explains the required grant.
Restore Accessibility and reopen the menu.
Hold one configured accelerator in another process, relaunch Tristr Flow, and confirm the menu warns that a shortcut is unavailable.
Release the accelerator, wait for the health repair interval or simulate resume, and confirm the warning clears.
expected_results: Permission loss and registration failure are never presented as healthy.
The menu action opens the appropriate recovery path.
Lost registrations are retried and recover without restarting the app.

tests.title: PostHog receives operational events without selected content
tests.user_story: As the product owner, I can measure shortcut reliability without collecting private clipboard or selected text.
setup_instrumentation: Use the configured PostHog project token and correct regional ingestion host.
Open PostHog Live Events or query the target project after running the app.
steps: Launch the app and invoke one successful shortcut read.
Invoke Read selected text from the menu.
Exercise an Accessibility-missing or selection-capture failure.
Inspect the resulting PostHog events and properties.
expected_results: Operational events include trigger, registration outcome, failure reason, app version, and platform where applicable.
No selected text, clipboard content, HTML, API keys, service tokens, or email addresses are sent.
Events use an anonymous installation identifier without creating person profiles.
proof_to_capture: PostHog Live Events screenshot or query result
